[quote=new_westmore;61293471]Hamza's prodding and poking stirs the criminal underworld of Brunswick. In the dark, news travels far faster than you think. Amid tight lips and refusals to talk about Rahat, word of Hamza's snooping and seeking spreads across the city, eventually reaching the ears of the man he was looking for. When hearing of this, Rahat instructed his men to bring this Brother Hamza to him, so he could beat this potential rival down like the weakling he assumed him to be.

Several more nights pass before Hamza is intercepted by the Brothers. Turns out, the grime in New Westmore can just choose to cling to you. After a heated fight in a dingy alleyway, Rahat's goons beat Hamza down, and throw his unconscious body into a van to drive him to their boss. 

...

Hamza's eyes slowly open. A gravelly, harsh voice speaks to him.

[i]"As-salaam alaiykum. Looks like our little friend has finally woken up, huh?"[/i]

He tries to move, but find that he can't. He has been bound to a chair by ropes and tape.

[i]"Don't try anything funny, brother. You're in my territory now - my land, my rules. I will f*cking pop you if you dare try to escape."[/i]

Hamza looks up. A single lightbulb dimly illuminates the room he and his captor are in. He then tries to look around, looking for a source, a person to attach the voice to. His captor is lingering in the shadows, just beyond the reach of the light.

[i]"So I hear you've been looking for a man called Isa Rahat, hm? You seem know who he is, right?"[/i]

Hamza nods. He doesn't want to speak a word until he knows its safe to do so.

[i]"Hm. If you were a hitman, then you clearly f*cking suck at your job. But, you don't seem to strike me as one at all, brother. If anything, you don't even look like you belong around here. No, you're a new face here, aren't you?"[/i]

Hamza nods again.

The voice continues. [i]"Well then..."[/i]

The captor steps into the light. His figure is imposing; a tall, burly 6 foot man with a bushy beard and bald, tattooed head. His eyes have a piercing stare that could frighten a bear and bring it to heel. In his right hand he holds a handgun, notched with what Hamza can only assume is a tally of all of his kills.

The man is none other than Isa Rahat himself.

[i]"Tell me more about yourself. Go on."[/i][/quote]
TERRORIST?! IN ARGOS?! NOT IN MY REGION!

[quote=irocco;61293596]Hamza thought briefly to his time as a younger brother selling in the hinterlands by the Iroccoan border. [i]"Brother, have you felt the sting of an Iroccoan lash? Have you seen scores of soldiers mowed down for resisting the black banner? It's flee or perish, and we have the humility to accept your leadership for our survival."[/i][/quote]
[i]"Yeah yeah, cut the dramatics, brother."[/i] Rahat leans forward, right up into Hamza's face.

[i]"I'll give you three weeks to prove to me that the Dharic family is legit. Bring your friends over with as much product as you can get, and meet me at the docks when you're ready. Fail to do that, and you and all of your friends are going to get popped the moment I catch you walking around in Brunswick, you hear?"

"Now, do we have a deal, brother?"[/i]

[b]Major Hockey League News[/b]

[b]Noosa team knighted[/b]

The vote for the team name, logo, colours, and even sweater design for the Noosa Hockey Association's newest Major Hockey League has come to an end. Out of 20,000 eligible votes, 56% voted for option 3, the Golden Knights. With this, the NHA have rebranded themselves as the Noosa Golden Knights and have adopted the logo of a steel gray and gold barbute-style helmet centered on a black shield, and have declared that steel grey, gold, red, and black are the official team colours. President of the NHA, George McPhee, held a press conference at T-Mobile Arena, the new home ground of the Noosa Golden Knights, in which he revealed the appointment of the first General Manger of the Golden Knights and the first signing.

Mr. McPhee announced that former Campbell River Flames defenceman Benjamin Moore has signed on as the first Head Coach of the Noosa Golden Knights. Moore was apart of the 2000s and 2010s dynasty that the Campbell River Flames established after appearing in nine playoffs, with Moore winning six Howe Cups, making him one of the most successful players in MHL history. Moore has said that he hopes to replicate this success with the Golden Knights and [b]"[...]establish the franchise as a dominant power heading into the 2030s"[/b].

The press conference also involved the reveal of the first trade made by the Golden Knights after a deal was reached with the Mary Sabers. The Mary Sabers acquired $5.5 million worth of cap space and a conditional 2028 3rd round pick from the Noosa Golden Knights for centre Colton Sissons and defencemen Jeremy Lewis.
[b]_____________[/b]

[b]Flames extinguish Jonni[/b]

The Chairman of Campbell River Sports and Entertainment, Nathan Murray Edwards, held a emergency press conference at Capbank Saddledome, Campbell River, Strath at 7:50 am December 31 after a emergency summons by the CRSE's board to Head Coach, Ryan Jonni. Much speculation had been placed on whether or not CRSE were going to renew Jonni's contract, which expires at the end of this season, following a tenure of eight years. In those eight years, Jonni failed to produce any notable results, with the Flames finishing last in the regular season four consecutive times and reaching the playoffs once in 2027. By the end of the 202526 season, many fans and even former players begun calling for Jonni to resign. A petition was even made, gathering 500 signatures to try and force his resignation. 

Now, with hopes of making the playoffs practically over following their 3rd consecutive loss last week (1 - 5 in favour the Courtenay Orcas whom are bottom of the table), the CRSE board has taken the initiative and elected to not renew Ryan Jonni's contract and instead have begun the search for a new coach with many suspecting they may poach Richard Clon, who's contract with the 2nd placed Parksville Penguins as Assistant Coach expires this season.
[b]_____________[/b]

[b]Battle of Qanuingittuq; Now with refreshments![/b]

With the recent addition of four teams in the Major Hockey League, the race for sponsorships has gone into full swing. One of these teams are the Oyster Harbour Blues, who have announced a partnership with Tooheys Brewery, a beer brewery centered in Oyster Harbour itself. Tooheys Brewery produce a variety of lager and dark ale since 1869, and have become a stable amongst households in the southern half of the island of Bascover.

Interesting enough, XXXX (pronounced 4-x) has announced a partnership with the Duncan Jets, the archrival of fellow state team, the Oyster Harbour Blues. With both teams based in the state of Qanuingittuq, the future games between them have been dubbed "the Battle of Qanuingittuq" when they play against each for the first time in the 202829 season. Now however, both Tooheys and XXXX are wholly owned by food and beverage company Lion, which bought the pair in 1992.
